name: Doria's Hawk
rangeDescription: New guinea, including and batanta (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A large, inconspicuous raptor of lowlands and foothill forest interior. Brown back and long tail with strong barring, pale underparts with strong sparse streaking, pale eye-brow and a thick dark eye-stripe.

name: Red-collared Widowbird
rangeDescription: Senegal and sierra leone eastward to southern south sudan and western uganda, southward to central angola, zimbabwe, zambia, mozambique, and eastern south africa
description: A small widowbird. The breeding male is jet black, with a crimson band across the breast, and a 20-centimeter floppy graduated tail.

name: Saffron-cowled Blackbird
rangeDescription: Paraguay to southeastern brazil, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Brightly colored blackbird. Males have a black nape and upper back; face, underparts, and rump are yellow tinged with orange.

name: Everett's Scops-Owl
rangeDescription: Philippines (bohol, samar, biliran, leyte, mindanao, and basilan)
description: A fairly small owl of lowland and foothill forest. Dark brown on the back with barred wing feathers, grayish underparts, a darker chest with black markings, a pale gray facial disk bordered with a black line, and pale ear tufts forming a V.

name: Plum-headed Finch
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (burdekin river, queensland to about sydney, new south wales)
description: Small brown bird with finely barred front. Brown above, paler and finely barred, below, with with pale spots on the wing and rump, pale-tipped tail, and tiny plum-colored cap (male also has plum-colored chin).

name: Magenta Petrel
rangeDescription: Chatham islands (population ±50 birds in 1992)
description: One of the rarest seabirds in the world, endemic to the Chatham Islands. Medium-sized bird with a distinctive dark gray head, neck, and upper breast and a gray chin.

name: Seychelles White-eye
rangeDescription: Forest of mahé and conception island (seychelles islands); reintroduced to frégate, cousin, and north islands
description: A small, sharp-billed warbler-like bird. Very dull olive-brown in coloration, with conspicuous white “spectacles.” Found locally in forest, woodland, and gardens on some of the granitic Seychelles islands.

name: Iberian Green Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Iberian peninsula and the pyrénées
description: Fairly large woodpecker with a green back, red crown, and broad whisker stripe (red in males, black in females). Yellowish rump shows mainly in slightly undulating flight.

name: Sumatran Leafbird
rangeDescription: Sumatra
description: Uncommon and declining Sumatran endemic, restricted to foothill forest at 600-1000 meters. A typical leafbird, with a predominantly bright green body in both sexes.

name: Black-winged Oriole
rangeDescription: Sierra leone and liberia eastward to northern and central democratic republic of the congo, southern south sudan, and western uganda, southward to northern angola; bioko island
description: A large oriole found primarily in secondary and submontane forests. Has a golden yellow body, a black head and throat, a red bill, and red eyes.

name: Sumba Buttonquail
rangeDescription: Sumba (lesser sundas)
description: A tiny, nearly tailless quail-like bird with a heavy bill, an orange-rufous chest patch, a pale whitish undertail, and dark, heavily streaked, cryptically patterned upperparts. Small groups inhabit native grasslands and scrub in lowlands and on low ridges.

name: Shelley's Francolin
rangeDescription: Southern uganda and southwestern kenya to northeastern south africa
description: Medium-sized, beautifully-patterned francolin. Shows rufous patches in the wings in flight.

name: Javan Blue-banded Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Java
description: Very rare, small kingfisher of forested streams and rivers up to the lower mountains. Highly threatened and found at very few remaining sites.

name: Night Parrot
rangeDescription: Arid interior of western and central australia (on verge of extinction)
description: Shy, elusive, and very rare nocturnal ground-dwelling parrot of inhabit arid environments, where it nests inside large spinifex clumps. Primarily green with yellow-green underparts and blackish markings throughout, less extensive than in longer-tailed Ground Parrot, in which adults have pale eyes (Night Parrot has dark eyes).

name: Raimondi's Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Western andes of peru (cajamarca to arequipa and moquegua)
description: Very local and nomadic in lower foothills of the Andes. Favors dry stony slopes and canyons, but ranges readily into nearby fields and scrubby areas.

name: Dark Batis
rangeDescription: Southern tanzania (north to the ukaguru mountains) southward to northern malawi
description: Males have the typical batis pattern of black, white, and gray. Females have a more unusual pattern, with rufous in the wing, rufous on the throat, and a variable amount of rufous on the breast.

name: Sooty Shearwater
rangeDescription: Breeds southern south america, new zealand, and southeastern australia; winters to north pacific and north atlantic
description: Medium-sized, dark brown shearwater with silvery flashes on underwings. Narrow wings with quick, deep wingbeats.

name: Timor Oriole
rangeDescription: Rote, timor, and semau (eastern lesser sundas)
description: Male is a distinctive oriole with a green head, dark mask, and orange-red bill. Duller female is brown above and paler below, with a dark mask and black bill.

name: Pink-breasted Lark
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern ethiopia to kenya, eastern uganda, and northern tanzania
description: An unusual lark with a slim bill and pinkish-brown markings on the face and underparts. Unlike many larks, shows no white in the outer tail or rufous in the wing in flight.

name: Long-tailed Silky-flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama (volcán de chiriquí)
description: Striking bird unlikely to be confused with any other species. Very long tail and obvious crest stand out, in addition to soft blue-gray body with yellow-green head and flanks.
